ranking_basis: Qualitative expected potential to improve spatially blocked HOLDOUT-DTI, balanced against implementation cost and data readiness. Rankings are judgments, not scores, deltas, calibrated forecasts, or evidence of performance.
novelty_scope: These are desk proposals, not an assigned lane or experiments. The proposed operators are not present in this repository's inspected current implementation, but related approaches exist in other projects. A pinned README-only scan of the nine focus repositories identified prior phase-congruency, radiometric K/Th and drainage work, so those earlier shortlist items were withdrawn; source-reported sibling results were not reproduced. hypotheses.title: Upward-continuation ridge trajectories in magnetic data
hypotheses.potential_label: Highest qualitative potential among these desk proposals; untested here
hypotheses.signature: Compute masked, edge-controlled upward continuations of the magnetic field at several declared heights, track the displacement and persistence of oriented ridge maxima across heights, and test a coherent trajectory rather than selecting one amplitude edge. Exclude or explicitly model FFT boundary and survey-seam effects.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A buried basement step can remain detectable in potential-field data where the surface fault map is incomplete. Variation across continuation heights may help distinguish broad source geometry, but does not prove a fault or its position.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: The local MSPTCD code uses multi-scale gradients and magnetic tilt, but not ridge trajectories across a separately computed continuation series. GEMSDOE32 already lists TMI_up150 in related methods, so this is a proposed extension of an existing family, not a claim of fleet-wide originality. The earlier phase-congruency idea is withdrawn because GEMSDOE32 reports an ARENA49-PCG implementation.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts, intrusive dikes, remanent magnetization, uneven survey height, leveling seams, and FFT edge artifacts.
hypotheses.data_status: Uses owner-mirrored magnetic and terrain bands, not authenticated organizer inputs. Continuation requires defensible units, nodata and boundary handling; no operator, canary, holdout or registry preflight was run.

hypotheses.title: Matched cross-flank texture displacement
hypotheses.signature: For independently detected candidate lines, search bounded two-dimensional translations between matched oriented texture windows on opposite flanks and require consistent displacement estimates across multiple window sizes; estimate nuisance statistics only on training regions.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A degraded or buried fault can offset a pre-existing magnetic or terrain pattern without producing a continuous mapped scarp; matched texture could suggest the missing line, but it cannot establish causation.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: The local implementation uses pointwise orientation and Hessian ridges rather than matched-window translation estimates. GEMSDOE28 lists a related two-sided texture-covariance idea as unimplemented and GEMSDOE24 lists a related texture-front proposal; this variant must not be described as wholly new to the fleet.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Intrusive boundaries, unconformities, erosional contacts, irregular textures and gridding seams can give apparent offsets.
hypotheses.data_status: Owner-mirrored bands were restored and hash-checked, not authenticated. Window quality, missing data, displacement ambiguity and fold-local controls have not been tested.

hypotheses.title: Focal-mechanism nodal-plane consistency
hypotheses.potential_label: Lower qualitative potential; external coverage unverified
layers: USGS ComCat focal-mechanism or moment-tensor products
local magnetic and terrain structural orientations, if independently derived
hypotheses.signature: For adequately located earthquakes, propagate both ambiguous nodal planes and hypocentral uncertainty into a broad spatial orientation likelihood, then test agreement with independently measured structural orientations; never treat epicenters or nodal planes as exact fault traces.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: Seismic ruptures can reflect concealed structures lacking a surface trace. Events with resolved mechanisms might provide orientation evidence where topography is subdued, if coverage and temporal representativeness are adequate.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: The inspected local implementation uses seismicity density and strain proxies, not explicit uncertainty-weighted focal nodal planes. GEMSDOE32 previously proposed a ComCat-related idea but reported it data-blocked, so the source and broader family are not new.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Induced seismicity, unrelated deeper faults, uncertain locations, catalog completeness changes, and the two-plane ambiguity.
hypotheses.data_status: Not viable here until specific event-product coverage, timestamps, quality and binary/API access are verified; no ComCat records were retrieved in this sandbox.

external_data.access_check: Official documentation describes a public event API, producttype filters for focal-mechanism and moment-tensor products, and event-specific associated products. This sandbox has not queried the target region or verified usable mechanism counts, access or competition sharing.

hypotheses.title: Groundwater-head discontinuity across aquifers
layers: USGS Water Data for the Nation groundwater-level and monitoring-location records
aquifer identity, observation time, reference elevation and uncertainty metadata
independent magnetic or terrain candidate orientations
hypotheses.signature: Compare coeval hydraulic heads from comparable aquifer depths on opposite sides of a candidate line, with uncertainty-aware discontinuity against a smooth regional groundwater gradient; require enough well pairs and do not interpolate sparse gaps into certain faults.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: Some faults restrict groundwater flow and produce head offsets even where alluvium hides surface expressions. The effect varies by aquifer and not all head discontinuities are faults.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: The inspected local implementation uses no matched hydraulic-head discontinuity. Historical heat-flow, springs and thermal/geochemical proximity experiments are related but measure different variables; unreviewed sibling implementations may still exist.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Pumping or recharge, irrigation, aquifer and depth changes, time offsets, stratigraphic barriers and datum errors.
hypotheses.data_status: Not viable until target-region well pairing, aquifer metadata, dates and machine-accessible bytes are checked. No data were downloaded here; modern API rate limits and possible free-key requirements must be checked for the eventual workflow.

external_data.source: USGS Water Data for the Nation modern APIs
external_data.access_check: Official USGS pages describe public groundwater and metadata APIs; modern services may require a free API key for more than a handful of requests per hour. Target-area coverage, water-level records and sandbox access were not verified.
